description:
The fifth READ reports '22', a duplicate key - the second of the two statuses that are an ordinary, non-fatal branch in the online programs and a fatal one here, and the half of gate G47 at this call site that its sibling case13 does not own. No other case in this folder reports '22' at any of the three I/O paragraphs. Like '23', a duplicate cannot arise from a sequential browse of an input file at all, and like '23' the program does not special-case it: app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl:L93 READ INTO is neither '00' at L94 nor '10' at L98, so the WHEN OTHER arm at L101 moves 12 into APPL-RESULT, the 88 APPL-AOK test at L104 fails, the 88 APPL-EOF test at L107 fails as well, and the shared fatal arm runs in source order - DISPLAY 'ERROR READING CUSTOMER FILE' at L110, MOVE CUSTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS at L111, PERFORM Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at L112 and PERFORM Z-ABEND-PROGRAM at L113. Because no arrangement of stored rows can make a sequential read report '22', the status is arranged on the input side by the scenario table in CBCUS01CParityTest rather than by anything in this file, and the two sides are written independently: this file states the output, that table states the backend, and the only place they meet is the cross-check on the rendered status line. The eight record lines that precede the failure are part of the expectation rather than noise. A mainframe spool holds whatever a job displayed before it abended, so a translation that buffered its output and dropped it on the abend path would be wrong, and the four delivered records account for eight lines rather than four because CBCUS01C displays every record TWICE - once at L96 inside the '00' arm of 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT and again at L78 in the mainline, with no statement between them that could change the record area, which is why the two lines of each pair are byte-identical and adjacent. That doubling is a genuine per-program inconsistency, preserved rather than harmonised (practice B5); de-duplicating it would halve every fingerprint this program produces. Each line is the raw 500-character group image byte for byte, including the 168 spaces of the trailing FILLER that app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy declares, and the images are the first four rows of the shipped fixture in ascending CUST-ID order, which is the order a KSDS browse keyed on CUST-ID PIC 9(09) reports them in. RETURN-CODE is 12, and it is derived rather than assumed: the value L101 moves is the value standing in APPL-RESULT when CALL 'CEE3ABD' is reached at L158, alongside MOVE 0 TO TIMING at L156 and MOVE 999 TO ABCODE at L157. It is L101 that supplies it here and not L124 - L124 is the open paragraph's fatal move, and this case's open succeeds. It is NOT 8, which is only the pessimistic pre-set L119 makes before the OPEN and which L122 overwrites on the successful open this case has, so it is never observable. It is NOT 16, which is APPL-EOF, an internal state reached only by a '10' read, and this run never reaches end of file. It is NOT 0, which only L87's GOBACK produces. Only 0 and 12 are derivable from this program at all. The literal NNNN in 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0022' is GENUINE EXPECTED OUTPUT and must not be 'corrected'. Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS codes DISPLAY 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' IO-STATUS-04 at both L168 and L172, and those four characters are placeholder text the original author never substituted: COBOL emits the literal verbatim and then appends the operand, so the emitted line carries the text NNNN and the four-character image together with no separator. A reader of this fixture should treat NNNN as inherited behaviour (practice B5) and never as a placeholder a case author left behind (practice B1). The value is rendered through the numeric branch, and both predicates of L162-L163 are false for it: IO-STATUS is all-numeric, so IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC does not fire, and IO-STAT1 is '2' rather than '9', so the OR arm does not fire either. The paragraph therefore takes its ELSE arm at L170-L172 - MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04, then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), overlaying the two status characters on the one-based positions three and four to give 0022. IO-STATUS-04 is read mechanically from the WORKING-STORAGE declaration at L57-L59 as IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 (practice B11). The code page is named explicitly rather than inherited from the platform (practice B8), and it matters in two different ways here. The eight record images are US-ASCII bytes decoded to 500 characters: the harness decodes with ParityHarness.FIXTURE_CHARSET, an explicitly named US-ASCII Charset, and app/data/ASCII is the ASCII half of the shipped data - the EBCDIC half is read as IBM037 and is not what this case seeds. The rendered status line, by contrast, is charset-independent in this case and only in this case, because the ELSE arm copies two characters and reinterprets no byte. Had IO-STAT1 been '9', the extended arm at L164-L167 would have run instead: MOVE IO-STAT1 TO IO-STATUS-04(1:1) puts '9' at position one, MOVE 0 TO TWO-BYTES-BINARY at L165 zeroes both bytes of the PIC 9(4) BINARY, MOVE IO-STAT2 TO TWO-BYTES-RIGHT at L166 drops the raw byte of that character into the low-order byte through the TWO-BYTES-ALPHA REDEFINES at L54-L56 so the binary's value becomes the unsigned value of the byte, and MOVE TWO-BYTES-BINARY TO IO-STATUS-0403 at L167 renders it zero-filled through PIC 999. Under US-ASCII a status of '90' would then render as '0' = 0x30 = 48 = 048, giving NNNN9048; under EBCDIC IBM037 the same status would legitimately render as 0xF0 = 240, giving NNNN9240. That arm is exercised in this folder by case10 (open '92' -> NNNN9050), case16 (close '96' -> NNNN9054) and case17 (the permanent-error convention, '9' followed by a zero byte -> NNNN9000), and those three are the expectations that must move if the charset binding ever moves. This one must not, and stating both facts here is what tells a future reader which is which. The message text names the file the long way. The read and close paragraphs say 'CUSTOMER FILE' at L110 and L147 while the open paragraph names the DD instead at L129, 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE'. The wording is inconsistent in the source and each paragraph's own literal is reproduced exactly; this case takes the read paragraph's. The closing banner at L85 is not emitted, and no close message of any kind appears. CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L158 terminates the enclave, so control never returns from L113 to its caller: the PERFORM 9000-CUSTFILE-CLOSE at L83 never runs and L85 is never reached. A case that appended that banner because the run had 'finished' would assert a line the abend makes unreachable, so the banner's literal text is deliberately absent from this file altogether, in the expectations and in this prose alike - a reader grepping the fixture tree for it will not find it here. expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are both empty and no expectedDatasets is declared, because this case arranges a backend failure and therefore meets a stubbed customer master rather than a stored relation: nothing is stored, no final state is read back, and none is reported. An empty expectation is a positive assertion that nothing was produced on that channel, so declaring the seeded rows as a final state here would assert output the arranged path never reports and would fail the diff. The clean-path cases, case01 chief among them, own the stored-state and dataset-level assertions. Nothing is written in any event: CBCUS01C opens CUSTFILE INPUT at L120 and issues no WRITE, no REWRITE and no DELETE anywhere. Six rows are seeded although four are delivered, which pins two separate things - the pass stops two records short of the end of the seeded file, so it is the abend and not exhaustion that ends it, and the seed is large enough for the arranged failing read to be the fifth read rather than the file's last. That is what distinguishes this case from case12, which seeds five and fails the fourth read, and from case13, which seeds four and fails the third. The dataset is addressed by the binding key CUSTFILE alone - the name L29's SELECT ASSIGN TO gives it and the name app/jcl/READCUST.jcl STEP05 mounts on its single //CUSTFILE DD - so the DSNAME stays in configuration and never appears in a case (gate G46). That step is a bare EXEC PGM=CBCUS01C with no PARM, so jobParameters is empty. custdata.txt matches its copybook width exactly at 500 bytes, so no normalisation is declared; only cardxref.txt needs the 36-to-50 FILLER pad. The unit kind is SERVICE: the harness constructs CustomerService and calls readAndPrintCustomerFileTo, which is the production streaming entry point and the shortest path to the decision logic there is, with no JobLauncher, no job repository, no application context and no HTTP layer anywhere in the path (gate G51). The four cases that abend inside the read paragraph are split deliberately across both entry points - case12 and case17 drive the tasklet of CustomerFileReaderJob, case13 and this case drive the service directly - so neither the batch wiring nor the decision logic is left asserted only indirectly over a fatal read arm. R1 caveat: the mandated names CustomerRepository, CustomerService and CustomerFileReaderJob describe a data-access helper and a job, but the source header reads 'Type : BATCH COBOL Program' and 'Function : Read and print customer data file' - it computes nothing and writes no dataset, which is why no output record is expected here and why the runnable batch form is preserved rather than dropped. Baseline provenance (practice B12): these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the control flow of app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl, the byte layout app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy declares, the step and DD contract in app/jcl/READCUST.jcl and the real 50-row app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt fixture. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution - running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, as AAP section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers, and the substitution of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. Gates discharged: G15 (one of the twenty cases this program owns), G18 (the diff count must be zero across all twenty before the module is complete), G35 (the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L158 surfaces as an AbendException carrying RETURN-CODE 12, which the step reports as a non-zero exit status), G47 (the '22' arm of the read's guard chain, the one status in the WHEN OTHER family no other case in this folder reports), G50 (88-level coverage in both states: APPL-AOK true at L126 on the successful open and true for the four delivered reads, false at L104 for the fifth; APPL-EOF false at L107 throughout, because end of file is never reached) and G51 (the decision logic is reached as a plain Java object, with CustomerService holding every branch this case drives).

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges a READ that fails after four records with a duplicate: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names READ-CUSTFILE and gives it FILE STATUS '22', reported after 4 record(s). It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the arrangement used to live in a table in CBCUS01CParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', so this file showed the rendered status and the abend and said nothing about what produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site runs the ordinary path, so silence here is itself a statement.
